# tests/unit/test_spec_001.py
from src.domain.difficulty import Difficulty


def test_selecting_beginner_gives_9_rows_9_columns_10_mines():
    # Given: the difficulty presets are available (Beginner is one of them).
    # When: the player selects Beginner.
    beginner = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Beginner")

    # Then: the preset's board is exactly 9 rows, 9 columns and 10 mines.
    # Rows: the Beginner preset fixes rows at 9 (the at-limit value).
    assert beginner.rows == 9
    # Columns: the Beginner preset fixes columns at 9 (the at-limit value).
    assert beginner.columns == 9
    # Mines: the Beginner preset fixes mine_count at 10 (the at-limit value).
    assert beginner.mine_count == 10


def test_beginner_rows_and_columns_stop_at_9_not_one_beyond():
    # Given: the difficulty presets are available.
    # When: the player selects Beginner.
    beginner = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Beginner")

    # Then: the board is not one step beyond the limit of 9 in either direction.
    # One beyond the limit would be 10 rows, which Beginner must not use.
    assert beginner.rows != 10
    # One beyond the limit would be 10 columns, which Beginner must not use.
    assert beginner.columns != 10
    # Only the 9-row, 9-column board is Beginner, so rows is strictly below 10.
    assert beginner.rows < 10
    # And columns is strictly below 10.
    assert beginner.columns < 10


def test_beginner_mine_count_stops_at_10_not_one_beyond():
    # Given: the difficulty presets are available.
    # When: the player selects Beginner.
    beginner = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Beginner")

    # Then: the mine count is not one beyond the limit of 10.
    # One beyond the limit would be 11 mines, which Beginner must not use.
    assert beginner.mine_count != 11
    # Exactly 10 mines is the limit, so the count is strictly below 11.
    assert beginner.mine_count < 11

# tests/unit/test_spec_002.py
import pytest

from src.domain.difficulty import Difficulty


def test_selecting_intermediate_gives_16_rows_16_columns_40_mines():
    # Given the difficulty presets are available (the preset table is built into the class).
    # When the player selects Intermediate.
    difficulty = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Intermediate")

    # Then the new game board has 16 rows.
    # The Intermediate preset fixes rows at exactly 16 (the value at the limit).
    assert difficulty.rows == 16

    # Then the new game board has 16 columns.
    # The Intermediate preset fixes columns at exactly 16, not the Expert value of 30.
    assert difficulty.columns == 16

    # Then the new game board has 40 mines.
    # The Intermediate preset fixes mine_count at exactly 40, not Beginner's 10 or Expert's 99.
    assert difficulty.mine_count == 40


def test_intermediate_preset_is_not_one_step_beyond_its_limits():
    # Given the difficulty presets are available.
    # When the player selects Intermediate.
    difficulty = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Intermediate")

    # Then the rows are not one step beyond the limit: the value is 16, so it is not 15 or 17.
    assert difficulty.rows not in (15, 17)

    # Then the columns are not one step beyond the limit: the value is 16, so it is not 15 or 17.
    assert difficulty.columns not in (15, 17)

    # Then the mines are not one step beyond the limit: the value is 40, so it is not 39 or 41.
    assert difficulty.mine_count not in (39, 41)

from src.domain.difficulty import Difficulty


def test_selecting_expert_gives_a_board_of_16_rows_30_columns_and_99_mines():
    # Given: the difficulty presets are available (the preset table is built into Difficulty).
    # When: the player selects the Expert preset.
    selected = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Expert")

    # Then: the Expert preset fixes the board at 16 rows.
    # Expert is defined as 16 rows, so rows must be 16.
    assert selected.rows == 16

    # Then: the Expert preset fixes the board at 30 columns.
    # Expert is defined as 30 columns, so columns must be 30.
    assert selected.columns == 30

    # Then: the Expert preset places 99 mines.
    # Expert is defined as 99 mines, so mine_count must be 99.
    assert selected.mine_count == 99


def test_expert_preset_is_exactly_at_30_columns_and_99_mines_not_one_beyond():
    # Given: the difficulty presets are available.
    # When: the player selects the Expert preset.
    selected = Difficulty.select_preset(name="Expert")

    # Exactly at the limit: 30 columns is accepted and the preset keeps that exact value.
    # The Expert preset has 30 columns, so the value equals 30.
    assert selected.columns == 30

    # Just beyond the limit: 31 columns would be a different board and must not be the Expert preset.
    # The Expert preset has 30 columns, so it is not 31.
    assert selected.columns != 31

    # Exactly at the limit: 99 mines is accepted and the preset keeps that exact value.
    # The Expert preset has 99 mines, so the value equals 99.
    assert selected.mine_count == 99

    # Just beyond the limit: 100 mines would be a different board and must not be the Expert preset.
    # The Expert preset has 99 mines, so it is not 100.
    assert selected.mine_count != 100

class Difficulty:
    """Difficulty."""

    @classmethod
    def select_preset(cls, name: str) -> Difficulty:
        """Build the difficulty preset registered under the given name.

        Args:
            name: The preset name, one of Beginner, Intermediate or Expert.

        Returns:
            A Difficulty holding the rows, columns and mine count of the preset.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the name does not match a known preset.
        """
        presets = {
            "Beginner": (9, 9, 10),
            "Intermediate": (16, 16, 40),
            "Expert": (16, 30, 99),
        }
        if name not in presets:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown difficulty preset: {name}")
        rows, columns, mine_count = presets[name]
        return cls(
            id=name.lower(),
            name=name,
            rows=rows,
            columns=columns,
            mine_count=mine_count,
        )
